name: Candito 6 Week

card.summary: A free six-week strength programme by powerlifter Jonnie Candito that cycles through accumulation and peaking phases to build strength and muscle for a stronger-looking physique.
card.note: Heavy barbell training carries ordinary lifting injury risks.

quick.overview:
The Candito 6 Week programme is a barbell strength routine created by Jonnie Candito, built around the squat, bench press and deadlift. It runs for six weeks, moving from a short accumulation phase to a peaking phase.

For looks, it is a way to add strength and muscle: more load over time supports more muscle on the frame. It is aimed at intermediate lifters, is distributed free as a spreadsheet and is often repeated or used between other programs such as 5/3/1.
quick.how: Lifters enter their current maxes into the spreadsheet, which calculates weights as percentages. It runs about four days a week with medium-high volume, finishing with a deload or one-rep-max testing.
quick.risks: Ordinary risks of heavy barbell training: strain or joint injury, especially with poor technique or too little recovery.

lead: The Candito 6 Week Strength Program is a six-week powerlifting-style programme designed by Jonnie Candito, focused on squat, bench press and deadlift.[1] A fitness-site description lists a short accumulation phase and a peaking phase, four training days per week, medium-high volume and a free spreadsheet.[2]

For appearance, such programmes are used to get stronger and thicker: progressive loading of the big lifts builds muscle, and some lifters on T Nation forum logs mention running it as a short beginner or return-to-training block before 5/3/1 or Sheiko.[3][4]
It is aimed at intermediate lifters with a competition 3 to 6 months away or a weak point, and is short enough to repeat.[2]

angle.text: The programme is a strength routine; the looks benefit is whatever muscle comes from consistent progressive training of the main lifts.

paras: The programme is distributed as a spreadsheet in which lifters enter their maxes and receive percentage-based weights.[2] Sources differ on frequency; one fitness site lists four days per week.[2] The final week is described as a deload or taper before testing maxes.[2]

On T Nation training logs, members mention planning to run Candito's free six-week programme as a short block before 5/3/1, or before a meet.[3][4] Another thread lists Candito among well-known strength YouTubers and programmers.[5]
